- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +1.09 to +1.13) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative (e.g., -1.13 or -0.41) — model fails to recognize downward momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term sentiment volatility — forecasts lag behind true price drops after negative sentiment.
- Mean reversion bias: model overestimates long-term price stability, ignoring recent sharp declines or rallies.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts often overpredict early in the period, then underestimate later — especially after sentiment shifts.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.31, 0.36), model tends to overforecast — treat as “false optimism” signal.
- Always adjust downward if sentiment history shows recent negative momentum (last 3–5 days) — especially if price has already fallen.
